title: Why the First Generations Lived Long: The Descent of Rule from Year to Moment
arc: The teaching answers why Adam and the ancients lived enormously long while we live briefly: in the beginning the powers ruling the cosmic circuit were the lords of the year (the inmost, most comprehensive degree), and as the ages have passed authority has descended through month, day, hour, and moment, so that the lifespan, stature, fertility, light, and life of human generations have shrunk in exact proportion to the descent of governance from inmost to ultimate.
reading:
The teaching opens with a question about Adam: how was he molded, how was he begotten, and is his begetting like the begetting of men today? The Apostle answers that there is a real difference, and the whole argument that follows is an answer to a single spiritual question — why was the first man "a strong one in his support, his stature great according to his other years," while we are small, short-lived, and feeble. The answer is given through the doctrine of the five powers that govern the sphere of the zodiac, and it is a teaching about the descent of human life through the discrete degrees from celestial to sensual.

The cosmological mechanism is this: in the sphere and the heavens above her there are five types of "powers and way-leaders," each named for a unit of time — the lord of the year, the lord of the month, the lord of the day, the lord of the hour, the lord of the moment. These are not five chronologies but five discrete degrees of governance in the natural-rational interface, the standard five-fold completeness. The year stands inmost (broadest, most comprehensive, most filled with light), and the descent year → month → day → hour → moment runs from the celestial through the spiritual and natural down into the merest ultimate. Each lower lord rules a smaller and more external register of natural life, and the rule of each in turn determines the quality of what is begotten under him. These powers received authority "from the beginning of the creation unto the end of the cosmos," so the whole arc of the ages is a single descending hand-off of dominion from the inmost cycle to the most outward.

In the first generations the lord of the year was reigning. Therefore the offspring of those generations partook of the year's amplitude: their lifespan was many years, their stature great, their support strong, their light and life abundant in the world. When that authority was completed, the lords of the months received it; their offspring were correspondingly smaller, "as the months are smaller than the years." Then the lords of the days, then of the hours, then of the moments — and at each handover the children begotten in the world shrank in measure with the unit that now governed them. We today are begotten under the lord of the moment, the bare ultimate, and so our days are short and our years diminished.

This is read correspondentially as the progressive externalization of the human race. The five lords correspond to the five faculties (mind, thought, teaching, counsel, reflection) under which natural life is held; when humanity stood under the inmost faculty, life and light flowed into the natural in fullness, and the body — being the form of love and wisdom in ultimates — received that fullness as long life and great stature. As governance fell to lower faculties, the channel narrowed; less life and light could enter the natural, and the body shrank to match its diminished influx. The teaching states this directly at the center of the chapter: "the life and the light were in the world in the first generations more abundantly than today's; for this very reason they have grown small in their support, and their lifetime has become small in their hand." The shortening of life is not biological accident but the registering, in ultimates, of the withdrawal of inner influx.

The teaching extends the same logic to fertility. The first generations brought forth not one child but five or seven in a single womb, and the earth was filled with them. This is the celestial signature of that earlier state: where the inmost rules, the matrix of life is fruitful in the fullness-of-five and the sabbath-fullness-of-seven, and many gathered truths or affections come forth conjoined in one receptive vessel. Today men are begotten one by one, or at most two or more in separate parts, and each emerges "another kind at a remove in their likeness, small in their stature, feeble in their members, their teachings and counsel filled with evil." The fragmentation of birth, the smallness of the body, the weakness of members, and especially the corruption of the third and fourth faculties (teaching and counsel filled with wickedness) are all the same descent read in different registers — the natural mind that no longer stands under the lord of the year stands under the lord of the moment, and what it begets is afflicted, miserable, ceasing from its standing, ending in "the other death" which is "bad — of darkness."

The arc therefore moves from a question about Adam's begetting to a cosmological doctrine of five governing degrees, to a chronological narrative of authority handed downward, to a final correspondential picture of the present human condition as a body, a lifespan, and a moral state shrunk to the size of the moment. The hidden teaching beneath the surface is that the magnitude of human life in any age is the magnitude of the heaven that rules it, and that the brevity, smallness, and corruption of the present generation is the outward sign that the natural has been cut off, by stages, from the inmost storehouse of life and light. The teaching does not promise reversal here; it only names the descent. But by naming it as a descent of governance through five discrete degrees, it implicitly points to the only remedy — the recovery, through regeneration, of life under the inmost lord, where years rather than moments measure the soul's stature.
